question: What is the very first segment of the small intestine connected to the stomach?
explanation: The duodenum is the initial C-shaped segment that receives chyme from the stomach along with digestive juices. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T4#GNS121_U1_T4_h1)

question: Where does the small intestine join the large intestine?
explanation: The ileocecal valve marks the transition point where the terminal ileum empties its contents into the cecum. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T4#GNS121_U1_T4_h1)

question: What are the microscopic projections on the surface of enterocytes called?
explanation: Microvilli form the brush border of intestinal absorptive cells, greatly increasing the surface area for nutrient uptake. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T4#GNS121_U1_T4_h2)

question: Why does the inner lining of the small intestine feature circular folds?

options.A: To produce mucus that protects against mechanical friction
options.B: To secrete strong hydrochloric acid for protein breakdown
options.C: To store solid waste until defecation occurs
options.D: To slow down chyme movement and increase absorption area

explanation: Plicae circulares force chyme to spiral through the lumen, ensuring it stays in contact with absorptive surfaces longer. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T4#GNS121_U1_T4_h2)

question: What are the three distinct bands of longitudinal muscle running along the colon called?
explanation: Teniae coli are longitudinal muscle strips that bunch the colon wall into distinct pouches known as haustra. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T4#GNS121_U1_T4_h3)

question: What is the primary function of the large intestine?

options.A: Producing the majority of digestive enzymes for proteins
options.B: Emulsifying dietary fats using synthesized bile salts
options.C: Absorbing water and consolidating waste into feces
options.D: Absorbing nearly all dietary carbohydrates and amino acids

explanation: The large intestine extracts remaining water and mineral ions from indigestible food residue, turning it into solid stool. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T4#GNS121_U1_T4_h3)

question: Which intestinal layer contains the submucosal nerve plexus?
explanation: The submucosa houses blood vessels, glands, and the submucosal nerve plexus which regulates glandular secretion. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T4#GNS121_U1_T4_h4)

question: What is the main function of the muscularis externa layer?

options.A: Anchoring the intestinal loops securely to the posterior abdominal wall
options.B: Providing motility through coordinated muscle contractions
options.C: Secreting protective mucus onto the epithelial surface
options.D: Absorbing digested amino acids directly into blood capillaries

explanation: The inner circular and outer longitudinal smooth muscle layers work together to generate peristaltic and segmenting movements. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T4#GNS121_U1_T4_h4)

question: Into which structure do digested dietary lipids primarily enter first?
explanation: Chylomicrons containing absorbed fats are too large for blood capillaries, so they enter the lymphatic lacteals inside the villi. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T4#GNS121_U1_T4_h5)

question: What role do bile salts play in fat digestion?

options.A: Chemically breaking peptide bonds within triglyceride chains
options.B: Emulsifying large fat globules into smaller micelles
options.C: Neutralizing acidic gastric juice entering the duodenum
options.D: Transporting fatty acids directly across the renal tubules

explanation: Bile salts break large fat droplets into tiny micelles, increasing the surface area for pancreatic lipase to digest them. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T4#GNS121_U1_T4_h5)

question: Where does venous blood from the intestines go immediately after collection?
explanation: Nutrient-rich venous blood from the intestines travels through the portal vein to the liver for processing before reaching the general circulation. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T4#GNS121_U1_T4_h6)

question: How does the parasympathetic nervous system affect intestinal function?

options.A: It relaxes the internal anal sphincter during resting states
options.B: It causes widespread constriction of mesenteric blood vessels
options.C: It increases digestive motility and secretions
options.D: It completely shuts down all nutrient absorption processes

explanation: Parasympathetic input, largely via the vagus nerve, enhances peristalsis and stimulates digestive enzyme output. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T4#GNS121_U1_T4_h6)

question: A patient two days post-abdominal surgery has no bowel sounds and abdominal distension. What condition is most likely present?
explanation: Absent bowel sounds and distension following surgery often point to a temporary halt in intestinal peristalsis known as a paralytic ileus. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T4#GNS121_U1_T4_h7)

question: Which clinical sign is most characteristic of a mechanical bowel obstruction?
explanation: Mechanical blockage forces the bowel to contract forcefully against an obstruction, causing cramping pain and reflex vomiting. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T4#GNS121_U1_T4_h7)
